issue.title: fix(infra): ssh tunnel listener timeout no longer affected by clock skew
issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where starting an SSH port-forward tunnel could hang indefinitely or time out immediately if the system clock was adjusted while OpenClaw was waiting for the local listener to come up. This could happen during NTP step corrections, VM/container pause-resume, or manual time changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/infra/ssh-tunnel.ts:waitForLocalListener` previously measured its polling budget with `Date.now()` (wall clock). Wall-clock skew breaks elapsed-time checks:

- A **backward** clock step made `Date.now() - startedAt` negative, so the `while` condition stayed true and the loop could poll forever.
- A **forward** clock step could make the elapsed time immediately exceed the budget, causing a premature timeout.

The fix replaces `Date.now()` with `performance.now()` (monotonic clock) and restructures the loop around a `deadlineMs` with `Math.max(0, remainingMs)`, ensuring the budget is measured against a clock that only advances. This matches the existing pattern in `src/infra/startup-migration-checkpoint.ts:447`.

## User Impact

SSH tunnel startup is now resilient to system clock adjustments. Operators using remote gateways over SSH should see fewer unexplained listener-timeout failures or hangs after suspend/resume or NTP sync on the host.

## Evidence

### Before fix

A standalone probe replicating the original `Date.now()` loop under simulated clock skew:

```
BROKEN backward skew (Date.now): aborted after 1001 iteration(s) — would hang forever
BROKEN forward skew  (Date.now): timed out after 0 iteration(s)
```

### After fix

The same probe with the monotonic deadline logic:

```
FIXED  (performance.now + Math.max(0,·)): timed out after 99 iteration(s)
```

### Validation

- `pnpm test src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts --run` — 13/13 passed, including the new regression test.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.infra.json --builders 1` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts src/infra/ssh-tunnel.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm format:check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern -- src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts src/infra/ssh-tunnel.ts` — passed.

Note: `pnpm tsgo:core:test` timed out after 10 minutes with no output in this environment; the targeted infra test shard typecheck completed successfully.

issue.title: [Improvement]: Separate problem statement from solution design
issue.body:
## Context

`create-issue` requires the Issue to state the solution before anything is investigated. Its authoring contract says to write `Scope` with "included work" (`skills/create-issue/SKILL.md:29`) and `Validation` as "commands" (line 31), and both presuppose a chosen approach. Neither `create-issue` nor `plan-issue` has any step that surfaces a decision to the requester or tests the Issue's `Context` as a hypothesis; `review-pr` carries that rule ("Ask the requester when criteria are ambiguous or conflict") and the two upstream skills do not. `plan-issue` advertises a "verified implementation plan" while its four sections verify only the shape of tasks, never whether the plan is the right one.

The cause is therefore established rather than suspected: the authoring contract forces approach selection before investigation, and no phase before review is permitted to ask.

Issue #232 shows the cost. Its `Out` list was written correctly as problem boundaries, but its `In` list was a plan — compare two tools, select one, remove the task, add "proportionate" validation — authored before any investigation. Three decisions were then resolved silently. The tool choice was fixed by a superseding plan comment with no request for a decision. The undefined term "proportionate" was interpreted into a 454-line check that was deleted before merge. The document's contents were prescribed by the plan and later cut from 188 lines to 82. A fourth decision, whether to drop the setup-state reporting that no replacement tool provides, was never surfaced at all and the capability loss reached `main` unflagged after ten review rounds.

Issue #236 also edits `plan-issue`, so the two must not be in flight at once.

## Goal

`create-issue` records the problem and `plan-issue` owns cause investigation, approach selection, and the decisions that require the requester's judgment.

## Scope

- In:
  - The authoring contract in `skills/create-issue/SKILL.md`: `Scope` `- In:` states the part of the system the problem covers rather than the work to perform, `Acceptance criteria` are approach-agnostic, and `Validation` states how the outcome is observed.
  - The planning stages in `skills/plan-issue/SKILL.md`: cause investigation that tests the Issue's `Context` as a hypothesis, decision surfacing with options and a recommendation, and naming undefined terms the acceptance criteria depend on.
  - The no-plan path in `skills/implement-issue/SKILL.md`, including a checkable exemption and its revocation during implementation.
  - The instructional comments in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/change.md` and the `create-issue` and `plan-issue` rows of `docs/skill-contract.md`.
- Out:
  - Changing the five required level-two headings, so `cmd/validate-issue-body` and its tests stay untouched.
  - Adding any repository check, Go command, or required status context.
  - Rewriting Issues that already exist, including #234, #235, #236, and #237.
  - Changing how `review-pr` and `merge-pr` detect scope drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `create-issue` instructs that `Scope` `- In:` states the part of the system the problem covers, not the work to perform, and that an unmade decision is never scoped as work.
- [ ] `create-issue` requires acceptance criteria that hold regardless of the approach chosen, and `Validation` that names how the outcome is observed rather than implementation commands.
- [ ] `plan-issue` verifies the Issue's `Context` as a hypothesis before deriving tasks, and reports a false premise instead of planning around it.
- [ ] `plan-issue` lists each decision with more than one defensible answer, with options, trade-offs, and a recommendation, presents them to the requester, and resolves them from the answers rather than by writing a choice into the plan.
- [ ] `plan-issue` names every undefined term the acceptance criteria depend on and either defines it or raises it as a decision, and its "verified" plan means premises tested and decisions resolved.
- [ ] `implement-issue` proceeds without a plan only when the Issue states an established cause and the change admits one defensible approach, states both conditions with evidence in the handoff, and stops and routes to `plan-issue` as soon as a decision with more than one defensible answer appears during implementation.
- [ ] Applying that exemption test to Issue #232 declines it, because the replacement tool admitted more than one defensible answer.
- [ ] `docs/skill-contract.md` describes `create-issue` as producing a problem statement and `plan-issue` as producing the investigated cause and chosen approach.
- [ ] No repository check, Go command, or required status context is added.

## Validation

- [ ] Run `mise run validate:all` from the repository root.
- [ ] Run `go test ./cmd/validate-issue-body/...` and confirm it is unchanged and passing, proving the five headings were preserved.
- [ ] Run `mise run check:skills` and confirm `gh skill publish --dry-run` accepts both changed skills.
- [ ] Run `mise run verify:fsl`, and `mise run mutate:fsl-changed` against the merge base when a specification changed, reviewing survivors.
- [ ] Rewrite Issue #232 against the new contract as a scratch exercise and confirm its `In` list becomes a problem boundary and its three silent decisions become surfaced decisions.
- [ ] Confirm `git diff --stat` shows no addition under `cmd/` or `internal/`.

- Migrates knowledge layer to `AGENTS.md` as sole content file (`CLAUDE.md` becomes a pure `@AGENTS.md` import); vendors the Beyonder toolchain (skills, hooks, commands, playwright-cli) into `.claude/`
- Generates `.claude/beyonder/{workflow,environment,stack,review,learnings}.md`; command baselines measured clean on both the main tree and a throwaway worktree
- Ports the port-parameterisation slice of #376 (not the date-format changes) so `docker-compose.yml` reads `${BACKEND_PORT}` etc. instead of hardcoding ports, and fixes a `container_name` collision that broke running two `docker compose -p` projects side by side — found while verifying the parallel-run recipe
- Small follow-ups found along the way: `docs/ai/workflow.md`'s `.pull-requests` → `.github-pull-requests` path fix, promotes the forms-vs-views side-effect rule (bug #333) to a Hard Rule in `AGENTS.md`, disables CodeRabbit's `auto_review` (superseded by the new `mr-review` skill)

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run coverage run -m pytest` — 295 passed, clean on both `@maintree` and `@worktree`
- [x] `uv run ruff check`, `uv run djlint apps --check`, `uv run python scripts/check_one_class_per_file.py --fail-on-multiple`, `uv run python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` — all clean
- [x] App booted via `docker compose`, logged in end to end (`admin@yamsa.local` → `/welcome/`)
- [x] Two `docker compose -p` slots (main tree + a throwaway worktree) verified running side by side without collision

Note: `.claude/beyonder/environment.md` documents that a fresh worktree currently 500s on missing frontend build output (`yarn build`) — a pre-existing worktree-bootstrap gap surfaced by this verification, not introduced by it.

issue.title: fix(infra): ssh tunnel listener timeout no longer affected by clock skew
issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where starting an SSH port-forward tunnel could hang indefinitely or time out immediately if the system clock was adjusted while OpenClaw was waiting for the local listener to come up. This could happen during NTP step corrections, VM/container pause-resume, or manual time changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/infra/ssh-tunnel.ts:waitForLocalListener` previously measured its polling budget with `Date.now()` (wall clock). Wall-clock skew breaks elapsed-time checks:

- A **backward** clock step made `Date.now() - startedAt` negative, so the `while` condition stayed true and the loop could poll forever.
- A **forward** clock step could make the elapsed time immediately exceed the budget, causing a premature timeout.

The fix replaces `Date.now()` with `performance.now()` (monotonic clock) and restructures the loop around a `deadlineMs` with `Math.max(0, remainingMs)`, ensuring the budget is measured against a clock that only advances. This matches the existing pattern in `src/infra/startup-migration-checkpoint.ts:447`.

## User Impact

SSH tunnel startup is now resilient to system clock adjustments. Operators using remote gateways over SSH should see fewer unexplained listener-timeout failures or hangs after suspend/resume or NTP sync on the host.

## Evidence

### Before fix

A standalone probe replicating the original `Date.now()` loop under simulated clock skew:

```
BROKEN backward skew (Date.now): aborted after 1001 iteration(s) — would hang forever
BROKEN forward skew  (Date.now): timed out after 0 iteration(s)
```

### After fix

The same probe with the monotonic deadline logic:

```
FIXED  (performance.now + Math.max(0,·)): timed out after 99 iteration(s)
```

### Validation

- `pnpm test src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts --run` — 13/13 passed, including the new regression test.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.infra.json --builders 1` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts src/infra/ssh-tunnel.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm format:check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern -- src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts src/infra/ssh-tunnel.ts` — passed.

Note: `pnpm tsgo:core:test` timed out after 10 minutes with no output in this environment; the targeted infra test shard typecheck completed successfully.

issue.title: Add SeedQR support for BIP39 passphrase input
issue.body:
## Description

### Problem or Issue being addressed

SeedSigner's passphrase QR workflow accepts plaintext UTF-8 QR codes, but does not accept Standard SeedQR or Compact SeedQR as passphrase input.

This PR adds the option to use either SeedQR format as a BIP39 passphrase while preserving the existing plaintext QR behavior.

### Solution

When scanning a passphrase QR, Standard SeedQR and Compact SeedQR payloads are detected and decoded using the existing SeedQR decoding logic.

Because SeedQR represents BIP39 word indexes rather than the original text formatting, decoded SeedQR passphrases are reconstructed canonically as lowercase BIP39 words separated by single ASCII spaces.

Plain UTF-8 passphrase QR input continues to preserve the exact text provided.

Malformed SeedQR input is rejected rather than being accepted as an empty or otherwise unintended passphrase. The passphrase scan workflow displays an "Invalid QR" warning when this occurs.

Tests cover:
- Standard SeedQR passphrase decoding
- Compact SeedQR passphrase decoding
- Equivalent Standard/Compact representations
- Preservation of existing plaintext passphrase behavior
- Malformed SeedQR rejection

Tested on a Raspberry Pi Zero W with physical SeedSigner hardware.

Using the same seed, I tested equivalent passphrases supplied as:
- plaintext QR

issue.title: De vulling loopt vast op 255 sockets, want elke notitie houdt er een open
issue.body:
Gemeten 2026-08-31 op de persoonlijke vault (2612 notities), plugin 1.13.7, server `app.knap.pantalytics.com`.

## Wat er gebeurt

Linken vult de cloud vault tot ongeveer 300 notities en staat dan stil. Geen fout, geen toast, geen voortgang meer. Negentig seconden meekijken op het tree-document: 297 paden, en het blijft 297.

## De meting

- cloud tree: 297 paden (284 `Dailies/`, 13 in de root), lokaal 2612 `.md`
- steekproef van 12 van die 297 documenten: allemaal gevuld, geen enkele leeg -- wat er staat is echt geland
- `lsof` op het netwerkproces van Obsidian: **258 ESTABLISHED verbindingen** naar de server, en dat getal beweegt niet meer

Chromium staat 255 websockets per renderer toe. Daarboven blijft de handshake in de wachtrij hangen in plaats van te falen.

## Waarom het dan alles stilzet

`VaultBinding.pushNote` doet `await synced` op de socket van elke notitie, en `KnapVaultClient` sluit een geopend document nooit. Notitie 256 krijgt geen socket, de promise resolvet nooit, en omdat `reconcileAll` in één queue loopt komt er ook niets meer achter langs -- geen file events, geen tree events.

## Wat eraan vastzit

Dit is niet één afterhandelbaar geval: één socket per notitie schaalt niet naar een vault van duizenden notities, hoe je de vulling ook batcht. Er is een keuze nodig over welke documenten live blijven (de geopende, plus de tree) en hoe de rest reist.

Raakt #106 (het scherm zwijgt tijdens het vullen) en #56 (de vulling meldt zich klaar terwijl er notities leeg blijven).

comment.body: Derde meting 2026-09-01: tijdens een lopende vulling (server groeide van 1569 naar 2120 paden in ~15 minuten) toont de settings-kaart "Up to date · 1,725 notes". De kaart meldt dus klaar terwijl de vulling nog loopt en eerder die middag definitief was gestokt op 1359 van 2611. Het omgekeerde probleem van de eeuwige *syncing*-kaart: geen van beide eindtoestanden is te vertrouwen zolang de vulling per sessie kan stokken.

The gate now says when a run is waiting on you.

Once CI went green the ci step kept polling until someone merged the PR, so the run stayed `running` and every reader showed a busy pipeline - a spinning `ci` in the status bar and an agent reporting "still working" while the gate was waiting on you.

- `enigma gate axi merge` merges the run's PR when you asked for it (`--method squash|merge|rebase`, `--force`), and `--merge` on `axi run` / `axi respond` does it as soon as CI is green. It goes through the scm layer on all three providers and refuses failing or unfinished checks, a closed PR, or a known conflict. The default is unchanged: the gate leaves the PR for you to review.

issue.body:
## What?
Builds on #79560.
PR also contains #81507. Can be shipped separately.

PR migrates the editor's Options menu from `DropdownMenu` to `Menu` from `@wordpress/ui`.

## How?

`@wordpress/ui` is bundled into each package instead of being shared as a script, so each package gets its own copy of `Menu` and its own React context. A component in `edit-post` cannot render a menu part into the menu the editor renders: the context it looks for belongs to a different copy, and the item throws. Every item in this menu therefore has to be rendered by a component that comes from the editor.

There are three kinds of items, and each gets there differently:

- Items in `edit-post` and `edit-site`, which fill the private slots of the menu. The editor exposes `MoreMenuItem` and `MoreMenuPreferenceItem` as private APIs, and those fills render them.
- Items of the plugins API. `ActionItem` now takes the component to render from the `as` the slot passes through `fillProps`, so the menu hands its own item component to every fill. Plugin authors keep using `PluginMoreMenuItem` and `PluginSidebarMoreMenuItem` as before.
- Items that pass an `as` of their own. Those keep rendering their component, wrapped so that they still take part in keyboard navigation.

## Notes

* Need to decide if we should log a warning for slots using a non-compatible `as` prop.
* Popovers opening from a new Menu don't properly return focus on close.
* Should we introduce a shared helper for keyboard shortcut representations in `@wordpress/keycodes` and `@wordpress/keyboard-shortcuts`, which would replace the local helper in the editor. 

## Testing Instructions
1. Smoke test the main Options menu in the post and site editors. They should function as before.
2. Test menu items from plugins - `test/e2e/specs/editor/plugins/plugins-api.spec.js` covers most of the cases.
3. Test Notes menu, which is implemented as a plugin sidebar.

### Testing Instructions for Keyboard
Same.

issue.title: Address accessibility issues from insight report: in main.js
RootValues drops contributing operands when a higher-order result is in the subtree

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issue.body:
Found while fixing #136, and deliberately left out of its scope.

## What happens

`RootValues` is documented as *"the metadata yielded by all results that evaluated"*. For a
composition whose subtree contains a higher-order result, it silently drops the metadata of operands
that plainly evaluated and plainly contributed.

Corpus seed 78 (`ResultTreeGenerator`), node
`greater than 2 & greater than 4 & (all neighbours == true)`:

```
node.RootValues            == ["n != k"]
causal leaves of that node == ["greater than 2", "greater than 4", "n != k"]
```

`greater than 2` and `greater than 4` are both causal operands of a satisfied `And`. They are not
reported.

## The boundary is exact

Over the Spec 3A corpus — 13,680 nodes across 150 seeds — `RootValues` was compared against an
independent descent of `CausesWithValues` down to the causal leaves:

| Nodes | Mismatches |
|---|---|
| Subtree contains a higher-order result | **2** |
| Subtree contains no higher-order result | **0** |

So the binary-operator / atomic-proposition core is correct, and every divergence involves
`Motiv.HigherOrderProposition.*`. The two mismatching nodes are the same logical node reached twice
by the corpus walk.

## Where it is likely to live

Not in the source walks — #136 corrected those, and this reproduces *after* that fix. The suspect is
`MetadataNode<TMetadata>.Resolve`'s collapse rule:

```csharp
return new Resolution<MetadataNode<TMetadata>>(children, childMetadata.SequenceEqual(metadata));
```

When `Collapse` is true the node's own tier is dropped and its grandchildren are spliced in.
A higher-order result expands one cause into many underlying tiers, so `childMetadata` for the
containing node is dominated by that expansion; the plain sibling operands' tiers appear to be
collapsed through and lost. `MetadataTier.Underlying` for the seed-78 node has 6 entries, all
traceable to the higher-order side.

## Relationship to #136

#136 fixed `UnderlyingMetadataSources`, which `MetadataNode.Resolve` calls, and that repaired
`RootValues` on **566 of the 13,680** corpus nodes — every one of them strictly gaining values it had
been dropping, none losing any. This issue is the residue that repair did not reach.

`Values` and `MetadataTier.Metadata` are unaffected in both cases — they read
`CausalResults.GetValues()` directly rather than going through the tier tree.

## Regression cover as it stands

`UnderlyingMetadataSourcesTests.Should_reach_every_causal_leaf_from_RootValues` asserts the invariant
across the whole corpus, excluding subtrees that contain a higher-order result, and names this issue
as the reason for the exclusion. Removing that exclusion is the acceptance test for this ticket.

## O que está mal

Ao adicionar uma despesa numa categoria dedutível, o valor 'dedução estimada' no ecrã Despesas soma corretamente a contribuição da despesa uma vez em memória (937,01 € -> 964,23 €, delta +27,22 €), mas ao recarregar a página soma a MESMA contribuição uma segunda vez (964,23 € -> 991,45 €, delta +27,22 € outra vez), inflacionando o valor final em +27,22 € acima do correto. A contagem de transações mantém-se corretamente em 13 em ambos os momentos (não há despesa duplicada), o que isola o bug ao cálculo da dedução e não à persistência da despesa em si. Testei com um loop de controlo de 4 reloads SEM adicionar nada e o valor manteve-se perfeitamente estável em 937,01 €, confirmando que a duplicação só ocorre associada à escrita de uma nova despesa, e que reloads subsequentes (testei mais 3) estabilizam no valor já inflacionado (991,45 €) sem continuar a subir.

## Como reproduzir

1. Abrir a app, ir ao separador Despesas, anotar o valor de 'dedução estimada' (baseline: 937,01 €, 29%)
2. Voltar a Início, tocar no FAB 'Adicionar despesa'
3. Preencher Montante '77,77', escolher categoria 'Transportes', tocar 'Guardar'
4. Ir ao separador Despesas: 'dedução estimada' passa a 964,23 € (30%) — correto, +27,22 € pela nova despesa
5. Recarregar a página (F5 / page.reload()) e voltar ao separador Despesas
6. 'dedução estimada' passa a 991,45 € (31%) — incorreto, subiu outros +27,22 € sem nenhuma despesa nova

## Esperado

Após o reload, 'dedução estimada' devia manter-se em 964,23 € (o valor já correto obtido antes do reload), pois nenhuma despesa nova foi criada entre o passo 4 e o passo 5.

## Observado

'dedução estimada' sobe de 964,23 € para 991,45 € só por recarregar a página, um aumento idêntico (27,22 €) ao aplicado quando a despesa foi criada — a contribuição da despesa de Transportes está a ser contabilizada duas vezes.

## Prova

1. /tmp/monthy-budget-team/critic-20260818-230534/functional/C-track-after-add.png (mostra 964,23 €, correto)
2. /tmp/monthy-budget-team/critic-20260818-230534/functional/dedu-after-add-final.png (mostra 991,45 €, após reload, incorreto)

4. output de consola do script de controlo t-dedu-reload-loop.mjs (sem adicionar despesa): 937,01€/29% constante em 4 iterações com reload

issue.title: salaries.csv: mls column mixes bare integers with day counts (15.2% of populated cells)

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

issue.body:
Found by the W3.5 spike (PR #944, docs/service-time-debut-clock.md). It is the
reason that spike ships a null rather than a finding, so it is already load
bearing.

## The finding

`scripts/data/contracts/salaries.csv`'s `mls` (major-league service time) column
holds two different notations in one column:

- **16,382 cells** use the `years.days` form, e.g. `4.078`.
- **2,926 cells** are bare integers, e.g. `1`.
- 19,308 populated cells in total, so bare integers are **15.2%**.

Counts confirmed independently by the orchestrator against the committed CSV.

A bare integer is ambiguous: it may be an exact figure or a rounded season
count, and the two share a spelling.

## What it costs

The W3.5 spike needed to know whether a player banked a full service year. On
men who provably banked none, day-count cells were wrong 0.6% of the time and
bare-integer cells were wrong 11 of 18. **State that as 11 of 18, not as 61%** -
the prevalence is solid, the error rate rests on a small provable subset and
should not be quoted as though it were measured across all 2,926.

More decisive: all 65 men who *could* have banked a year read a bare `1`.
Confirmations and errors share a spelling, so the column cannot settle the
question either way.

## Related, and already documented

Ground truth already records that `mls` is blank on every row before 2010, which
makes the 29.4% blank rate an era window rather than a discriminator. This is a
second, separate problem with the same column: the populated cells are not one
notation.

## What "done" looks like

Decide whether a bare integer can be disambiguated at all - possibly by checking
it against a day count derived from roster dates. If it can, parse to an
explicit `{ value, precision }` rather than a number, so a caller can tell an
exact figure from a rounded one. If it cannot, record in
`docs/contracts-data-caveats.md` that `mls` will not carry a service-year test,
so the next spike does not rediscover this the hard way.

Do not delete or rewrite a CSV row. `rowKey` is positional - see issue #931.

## Summary

Calling profiles can disable filesystem tools on `delegate_research` workers without cloning a second researcher profile.

- New `deep_research.worker_file_tools` (default `true`) is frozen onto `request.json` at `start`.
- Default path is unchanged: lanes inherit the researcher profile (`web`, `browser`, `file_readonly`); synthesis and correction stay `-t file_readonly`.
- When `false`: lanes run `-t web,browser`; synthesis and correction run `-t research_writer` (a sealed empty toolset: no retrieval and no files). Lane reports are already in the synthesis prompt.
- Invalid frozen requests fail terminally before any worker starts. Valid pre-flag jobs that lack only the new field retain the historical default.
- Sealed toolsets ignore plugin registry overlays. Ordinary toolsets keep their existing extensible behavior.

No profile names are hardcoded. Operators set the flag on the locked-down calling profile.

## Test plan

- [x] `HERMES_PYTHON=/root/hermes-agent/.venv/bin/python bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/deep_research/`

issue.body:
## Problem

src/components/ClaimableBalanceCard.tsx BalanceRow.handleClaim (lines 22-30) handles the result of claimBalance with:

  const { error } = await getClient().account.claimBalance(cb.id);

The else branch is entirely missing. When claimBalance returns an error string, the button simply re-enables and nothing happens — users receive zero feedback about what went wrong. Additionally, if the API returns { data: null, error: null } (which is valid per the SorokitClient type), setClaimed(true) fires with no real confirmation that the ledger operation succeeded.

Two more related problems: (1) after a successful claim the row stays visible with a 'Claimed' badge but is never removed from the list, so the count badge in the card header remains stale; (2) there is no loading guard preventing a second Claim click while the first is still in-flight.

## Solution

Add a local claimError state to BalanceRow and display it inline on failure. Verify data is non-null before setting claimed. Lift a removal callback from the parent so the claimed row is removed after success. Disable the Claim button while claiming is true.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A failed claimBalance call shows an inline error message below the Claim button
- [ ] claimed is only set to true when data is non-null (confirmed ledger result)
- [ ] Successfully claimed row is removed from the visible list
- [ ] The header count badge updates to reflect remaining claimable balances
- [ ] The Claim button is disabled while a claim is in-flight
- [ ] Claiming one row does not affect other rows in the list

## Purpose

Evaluate whether LGFC can add Cloudflare AI Agents as repository-working implementation/operations agents using **Cloudflare Free only**, with **no prepaid AI credits, no Workers Paid upgrade, no paid-only model, and no automatic billable overage path**.

The evaluation must prove both:

1. **agent quality** — a Cloudflare-hosted agent can correctly execute bounded LGFC repository work under existing repository authority; and
2. **runtime value** — Cloudflare Workers + Agents SDK + Durable Objects provide a useful, controllable execution environment for LGFC agent work.

This project does **not** redesign the LGFC repository workflow. GitHub Issues/PRs, repository authority, team queues, agent claims, builder/reviewer separation, required CI, review, merge, post-merge verification, evidence, and closeout remain unchanged.

## Product Authority direction

Initial evaluation is **zero incremental cost**.

Required cost boundary:

- Workers plan: Free
- Agents SDK: allowed
- Durable Objects: Free, SQLite-backed only
- Workers AI: free daily allocation only
- Paid Workers plan: prohibited for this evaluation
- AI Gateway Unified Billing / prepaid credits: prohibited
- paid-only Workers AI models: prohibited
- external paid LLM APIs: prohibited unless separately authorized later
- automatic billing/overage enablement: prohibited

If any required capability would cross this boundary, **stop and report the requirement**. Do not silently enable billing, purchase credits, upgrade a plan, or add a paid provider.

## Existing Cloudflare credentials

LGFC already has repository secrets representing:

- Cloudflare API token
- Cloudflare account ID

Implementation must first inspect the existing secret names and permissions.

Do not create duplicate secrets solely because Cloudflare examples use the environment-variable names:

- `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`
- `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`

A GitHub workflow may map existing secret names into the environment-variable names expected by Wrangler.

If the existing token lacks the minimum permissions required for the isolated evaluation Worker/Agent, stop and identify the exact missing scope. Do not broaden credentials without Product Authority approval.

No secret values may be written to Issues, PRs, repository files, logs, or durable documentation.

## Initial architecture

The first implementation should be isolated from the current website deployment and Production resources.

Conceptual target:

```text
LGFC GitHub
    |
    | authorized Issue / explicit evaluation dispatch
    v
GitHub Actions
    |
    | existing Cloudflare credentials mapped for Wrangler
    v
Isolated Cloudflare Worker
    |
    +-- Agents SDK
    +-- Workers AI binding
    +-- SQLite-backed Durable Object
            |
            +-- one named CF Agent instance / isolated state
```

The evaluation Worker must not become part of the existing LGFC website deployment path merely because both are hosted in Cloudflare.

## Agent-instance model to prove

One implementation Agent definition may support multiple simultaneous task instances.

Example:

```text
CFImplementationAgent / issue-A
    +-- Durable Object A
        +-- isolated state/workspace

CFImplementationAgent / issue-B
    +-- Durable Object B
        +-- isolated state/workspace

CFImplementationAgent / issue-C
    +-- Durable Object C
        +-- isolated state/workspace
```

The evaluation should prove that concurrent assignments remain isolated and do not create branch, workspace, state, or repository collisions.

## Repository authority boundary

Cloudflare is an **execution runtime**, not a new governance authority.

A CF Agent must operate under the same LGFC process as any other implementation agent:

```text
Issue
-> correct team queue / authorized lifecycle
-> eligible agent claim or explicit assignment
-> load repository constitution/authority
-> branch / bounded implementation
-> build / test
-> PR
-> deterministic gates
-> independent review
-> approval / merge
-> post-merge verification
-> evidence
-> Issue reconciliation / closeout
```

Running inside Cloudflare does not exempt the agent from repository authority.

## Initial authority for CF Agent

During bootstrap/qualification, the CF Agent has **no standing repository mutation authority**.

Initial permitted behavior:

- receive explicitly selected Issue/repository context;
- read repository authority and allowed files;
- reason about the task;
- execute bounded tests in its isolated runtime;
- produce an evaluation result;
- record usage/runtime evidence through the authorized calling workflow.

Initial prohibited behavior until qualification succeeds and a later bounded child authorizes it:

- claiming arbitrary Issues;
- creating branches;
- writing repository files;
- pushing commits;
- opening PRs;
- approving/merging PRs;
- changing GitHub settings;
- Production deployment;
- credential mutation;
- paid-service activation.

## Model selection

Use only a Workers AI model currently available on the Free plan.

Before implementation, verify current model availability from Cloudflare documentation rather than assuming a previously free model remains free.

The initial model is an evaluation variable, not a permanent LGFC architectural commitment.

## Evaluation phases

### Phase 1 — Free-tier account/runtime qualification

Prove without repository mutation:

- existing account ID and API-token path works;
- isolated Worker deploys;
- Agents SDK initializes;
- SQLite Durable Object initializes;
- Workers AI inference succeeds using a free-compatible model;
- Agent state persists across multiple invocations;
- daily/resource usage is observable;
- reaching a free limit fails closed rather than silently creating billable usage;
- disable/rollback path is documented and tested.

### Phase 2 — Repository comprehension test

Give the CF Agent one completed/bounded LGFC Issue plus:

- repository authority chain;
- relevant code/docs;
- exact starting commit identity;
- explicit no-write boundary.

Evaluate whether the Agent:

- reads and follows authority correctly;
- understands the Issue;
- distinguishes deterministic CI work from AI work;
- proposes a technically valid implementation/review;
- respects holds, lifecycle, scope, and protected decisions;
- avoids inventing authority;
- produces useful evidence.

### Phase 3 — First real bounded repository assignment

After Phases 1-2 are accepted, authorize one bounded implementation assignment through a child Issue.

**Preferred candidate assignment:** work from **#3633 — CI qualification, test catalog, consolidation, and Day-2 operational readiness**, after #3633 has completed enough inventory/deduplication/gap analysis to identify a clearly defined missing or deficient CI capability.

This relationship is deliberate:

- #3633 owns the question **what deterministic CI should exist**;
- this project proves **whether a CF Agent can implement that already-defined work**;
- the CF Agent must not create duplicate CI or substitute AI for a deterministic control that belongs in GitHub Actions/CI.

A suitable first assignment should be:

- bounded;
- non-Production;
- well specified;
- independently testable;
- low collision risk;
- useful even if the CF Agent evaluation stops afterward.

### Phase 4 — Full Issue-to-PR qualification

If Phase 3 succeeds, prove the complete standard agent workflow:

```text
assigned Issue
-> CF Agent instance / isolated DO state
-> clone/workspace
-> branch
-> edit
-> build/test
-> push
-> PR
-> LGFC CI/gates
-> independent review by an agent that did not implement
-> merge through existing authority
-> post-merge validation
-> evidence / closeout
```

Do not grant the CF Agent approval authority over its own work.

### Phase 5 — Parallel-capacity pilot

Only after a single full workflow succeeds, test multiple concurrent implementation instances on collision-safe Issues.

At minimum evaluate:

- two or more CF implementation instances concurrently;
- independent state/workspaces;
- separate branches/PRs;
- repository/GitHub API contention;
- CI load;
- failures/retries;
- cost/neuron/resource consumption per Issue;
- impact on PR quality and exception rate.

## Evaluation metrics

Capture at minimum:

- task completion correctness;
- repository-governance adherence;
- build/test success;
- first-pass CI/gate success;
- review findings / remediation count;
- post-merge exception count;
- runtime failures;
- retries;
- hallucinated/invented scope or authority;
- Workers AI neuron consumption;
- Worker/DO request and compute usage;
- elapsed execution time;
- human/senior-agent intervention required;
- estimated cost if the same workload later exceeded Free limits;
- comparison with existing implementation-agent experience where comparable.

## Potential future LGFC roles — evaluation only

If the platform is successful, future design may evaluate CF Agent roles such as:

- PMO Active implementation agents;
- Tier 1 Operations agents;
- repository documentation creation/maintenance;
- as-built vs documented-state reconciliation;
- deterministic CI opportunity discovery from recurring logs/failures;
- routine remediation implementation;
- evidence collection and validation.

These are **future role candidates only**. This project does not grant those standing roles automatically.

The intended long-term operating hypothesis is:

```text
LGFC senior agent team
  -> Governance
  -> Engineering research/qualification
  -> PMO Pipeline design and launch packages
  -> independent PR review
  -> Production promotion decisions

CF implementation pool
  -> bounded PMO Active implementation
  -> Tier 1 Operations
  -> routine repository/documentation work

GitHub Actions / CI/CD
  -> deterministic validation, monitoring, deployment, reaction, and evidence
```

The evaluation should determine whether this division improves throughput, separation of duties, quality, and cost.

## Separation of duties

A major target benefit is permanent builder/reviewer separation.

If CF Agents become implementation agents:

- CF implementers do not approve their own PRs;
- Cursor and/or Claude may independently review CF-created work where current governance permits;
- Product/Production authority remains unchanged;
- deterministic CI remains an independent gate surface.

## Relationship to #3633

#3633 remains the authoritative project for:

- defining the complete CI/test catalog;
- inventorying existing CI/tests;
- deduplicating/consolidating current CI;
- identifying gaps;
- building only missing/deficient deterministic CI and Day-2 capability.

This Cloudflare project must not duplicate #3633.

Instead, after CF Agent qualification, #3633 may provide one or more bounded implementation assignments to CF Agents as an execution method.

Grok remains the current preferred owner of #3633 unless Product Authority explicitly changes that assignment.

## Non-goals

- Chatterbox design or integration.
- Replacing GitHub as source of truth.
- Replacing repository governance with Durable Object state.
- Automatically eliminating current paid or free LGFC agents.
- Automatically replacing Cursor, Claude, Work, Grok, Codex, or other current agents.
- Enabling paid Cloudflare AI services during evaluation.
- Moving the LGFC website deployment into the Agent evaluation Worker.
- Granting autonomous Production authority.
- Automatic merge or self-approval.

Any future agent-team reduction or subscription change must be based on measured CF Agent quality, throughput, reliability, governance adherence, and cost.

## Deliverables

1. Free-only Cloudflare Agent architecture and cost guardrail.
2. Existing credential/permission assessment without exposing secrets.
3. Isolated Worker + Agents SDK + SQLite Durable Object evaluation runtime.
4. Free-compatible Workers AI model selection evidence.
5. Runtime/state/inference qualification evidence.
6. Repository comprehension evaluation.
7. One bounded real Issue-to-PR implementation pilot.
8. Independent PR review evidence.
9. Parallel-agent pilot if single-agent qualification succeeds.
10. Usage/cost/quality scorecard.
11. Recommendation: reject, retain as bounded tool, adopt as implementation pool, or expand through a separately approved project.
12. Rollback/disable procedure leaving the existing website and agent workflows unaffected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No prepaid credits or paid Cloudflare AI service are enabled by this project.
- [ ] No paid-only Workers AI model is used.
- [ ] Existing secret names are reused/mapped where possible; duplicate secrets are not created merely for naming conformity.
- [ ] API token permissions are least-privilege and any required expansion is surfaced for Product Authority approval before change.
- [ ] Agent Worker/runtime is isolated from the existing website deployment.
- [ ] SQLite-backed Durable Object Agent state works on Free.
- [ ] Workers AI inference works within the Free allocation.
- [ ] Free-limit behavior fails closed without silent billing.
- [ ] Agent demonstrates repository-authority comprehension before receiving write authority.
- [ ] First real assignment is bounded and separately authorized.
- [ ] #3633 is used as the CI authority rather than duplicated.
- [ ] Agent-created PR follows the existing LGFC PR workflow without special bypasses.
- [ ] Implementer/reviewer separation is preserved.
- [ ] Post-merge evidence and exception rate are captured.
- [ ] Parallel instances are tested only after single-agent success.
- [ ] Cost/usage per assignment is captured well enough to inform later team-capacity/subscription decisions.
- [ ] Existing LGFC agent team remains intact during evaluation unless separately changed by Product Authority.

## Current disposition

PMO Pipeline / evaluation project.

Prepare the free-tier architecture and bounded implementation package first. No Cloudflare deployment, repository write authority, paid-service activation, or Production mutation is authorized by this parent Issue alone.
